candidate_windows.window_text:
To fine-tune the T5 models (Raffel et al., 2019) we use the T5X framework (Roberts et al., 2022). We use the T51.1 and Flan-T5 checkpoints and train the models on TPUv4 chips, other than the "large" or smaller Flan-T5 models that used TPUv3 chips. We trained the models for up to $25\mathrm{k}$ steps with a batch size of 32 and learning rate of 1e-3 with the Adafactor optimizer (Shazeer and Stern, 2018). For reference, training Flan-T5 base on 4 TPUv3 took 1.5 hours. For each model, we picked the best checkpoint according to the ROUGE-L score on the validation set. We did not perform any hyperparameter tuning, and only retrain the T5-XL once with a new random seed, since the first training run of that model led to low training and validation scores.

Our few-shot evaluations are querying variants of the PaLM2 model (Google et al., 2023), which is available via API calls. We use temperature 0.0 to increase factuality. An example of our QuoteSum prompt with the preceding instructions and two retrieved demonstrations is provided in Table D.2. We also include the respective QSum-S prompt

in Table D.3, which includes QuoteSum examples that were automatically converted to have ALCE-style sentence-level citations instead of span-level quotes, and has the light ALCE (Gao et al., 2023) prompt instructions and formatting.
